idiom_name: service struct of trait ports + one owned sqlx Transaction, Result-based errors
implementation_notes: Idiomatic Rust has no dependency-injection container and no ORM-managed unit of work: the service is a struct generic over, or holding trait objects of, its repository ports, and the use case opens exactly one transaction with pool.begin().await?, passes &mut *tx (which implements Executor) to every repository, and finishes with tx.commit().await?; dropping an uncommitted Transaction rolls back. What replaces the classic structure is ownership: the transaction is a value the use case owns rather than a framework-managed context, dependencies are wired by hand at startup, and errors travel as Result with ? and a typed error enum (thiserror/anyhow). The hand-written form is the only form - the ceremony is real, not accidental.
pitfalls: A repository that takes the pool instead of the transaction silently runs outside it; pass &mut *tx (or a generic Executor) to every call in the use case.
A path that returns early with ? leaves the rollback to Drop; a forgotten commit is a silent rollback, and an .await in between can hold the connection for a long time.
Async trait objects require boxing (async_trait or RPITIT): generic services avoid the allocation but infect every caller's type signature with the port types.
